observations: The generated Hebrew modules have no metegs at all. The print marks stressed penultimate syllables with a meteg-like stroke throughout (segolates, -ֵנוּ, -ֶיךָ, -ִיתָ). All of these should be checked at full resolution before they are bulk-applied.

Resolution limit: the page JPGs are 1368 px wide and the bands are only about 1.4× enlarged, so letters are about 40 px tall. Strokes and vowel shapes are mostly legible. Interior dagesh dots in ס, מ and ל, and sheva in the יי Names, are not reliably legible. I did not certify those.

All English modules match s103 and s105 word for word except the missing comma in Hakol yodukha. Case (Hayoth, Merkabah, Seraphim, Ophanim, Owner, Kingdom, Name, Holy Sabbath) and British spelling (honour, splendour, lustre, fulfil) match the print.
The Hebrew cue words in the English (המאיר, הכל יודוך, אל אדון, לאל) are linkage cues. They are correctly left out of the translation text.
On s102 there is a stray high mark before מִימוֹת in the Sabbath paragraph, and a broken 'f' in 'of' on s103. Both are print noise and need no encoding.

Routing and placement match the print: weekday המאיר → אל ברוך above the rule; Sabbath rubric → הכל יודוך → אל אדון (with the repeated 'אַם שַׁבָּת.' / 'On Sabbath.' at the top of p. 38 before זְכוּת) → לָאֵל אֲשֶׁר שָׁבַת.
